text:
ara: quick nsys question — I profiled a failing KV-cache workload and see a ~40ms gap between when our prefetch NVTX span finishes and when the CUDA kernels actually run. timeline shows cuMemcpyAsync and then nothing for a bit, then a burst of kernels. suspect sampling/capture flags are hiding short host-side scheduling. any tips?

jay: that sounds like sampling window + capture-range alignment. if your capture is short or sample window is coarse you'll miss short CPU wakeups (OSRT threads) that schedule kernels. what flags did you use?

ara: ran: `nsys profile --trace=cuda,nvtx --output=out.qdrep --capture-range=nvtx:pf_start:nvtx:pf_end --sample=cpu --duration=5s`

marta: two quick notes: (1) include osrt in trace: `--trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt` so nsys records the OS runtime thread activity; (2) increase sample rate / duration or use continuous capture for the critical window. sampling only captures periodic stacks so you can miss short blocking points.

jay: also try `--sample=cpu` vs `--sample=gpu` depending on whether you want CPU stacks vs GPU counters. for scheduling gaps you want CPU stacks + osrt. add `--sample-interval` if available to tighten sampling.

ara: nice — i added osrt and extended to 12s, still seeing the gap but now NVTX shows our "prefetch_done" span ending 42ms before the first kernel. could kernel launch be deferred because of stream ordering or pinned memory copy scheduling?

marta: yep, stream ordering + cudaStreamSynchronize hidden on another thread can cause that. open the timeline, filter by API (cudaRuntime) and look for `cudaLaunchKernel` vs `cudaMemcpyAsync` calls and the associated thread lanes. often the cudaMemcpy is queued on a different host thread and the actual kernel launch happens on a separate CPU worker — check osrt thread lanes.

jay: if you suspect prefetch, also inspect Unified Memory migration ops: `cudaMemPrefetchAsync` shows up as API calls. if those migrate pages, the kernel might block until migration is complete. check memory activity in the GPU timeline.

ara: good call — i see some `cudaMemPrefetchAsync` on a host worker that finishes, but the migration appears fragmented. is there an nsys flag to capture page-faults or migration details?

marta: not directly page faults, but `--trace=osrt,cuda,nvtx` plus host sampling will show the worker doing migration. also export an sqlite: `nsys profile -o out --trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt --sample=cpu --sample-interval=5ms` then open in Nsight or run `nsys stats out.qdrep` to get timeline tables.

jay: one more trick: use `--capture-range=nvtx:pf_start:count=1` capturing exactly from your prefetch NVTX tag start to the next matching event; that avoids missing the tail if your outer harness has lots of noise. also avoid very short `--duration` (like <1s) — some kernels are very bursty and you'll miss them.

ara: here's the minimal repro command i'm going to try:

```
nsys profile \
  --output=pf_repro \
  --trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt \
  --sample=cpu \
  --sample-interval=5000us \
  --capture-range=nvtx:pf_start:nvtx:pf_end \
  --stop-on-duration=20s
```

marta: looks good. if you still see the gap, try disabling async prefetch (force synchronous copy) to confirm it's a scheduling/migration behavior vs a kernel selection/quantization delay. compare timelines side-by-side.

perf-bot: automated hint — export raw tables for quick grep: `nsys export --output=pf_repro.sqlite pf_repro.qdrep` then `sqlite3 pf_repro.sqlite "select timestamp, name, category from events where name like '%cudaMemcpy%' or name like '%cudaLaunch%';"`

ara: thanks everyone — running this now. will share trimmed qdrep if we need to dig into kernel durations and potential scheduling hotspots. :thumbsup:

jay: if you post the qdrep i can do a quick hotspot pass (kernel times by name, split by stream) and check if kernel selection is varying across batches which could explain delayed launches.

marta: and if you find repeated tiny memcpy spikes before kernels, consider batching prefetch calls or coalescing pages — that reduces migration fanout and host wakeups.

ara: sweet. uploading results in ~30m.
